newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore urged to guard against Thai-style crisis.
newsitem.headline: Singapore urged to guard against Thai-style crisis.

text.p: Thailand's recent currency problems must never be allowed to happen in Singapore, Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong was quoted on Sunday as saying.
Speaking at a dinner, Lee said the recent plunge of the Thai currency was a result of too much overseas borrowing and overbuilding in a property boom, the Sunday Times reported.
"The baht is down, there is a crisis of confidence and economic growth is affected," he said.
Lee added that long-term prospects for Thailand were still good but it was not easy to restore confidence after such a serious crisis.
"We must never let this happen to us," said Lee, son of Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew.
Lee stressed the importance of learning from the experiences of other countries in the region, pointing out that the Singapore dollar has also weakened in the wake of the Thai baht's fall.
Thailand floated the baht early last month in response to repeated attacks on the currency by speculators.
The baht had for years been tied to a fixed basket of currencies and the action resulted in a de facto devaluation.
By late July, the Singapore dollar had slid to a 32-month low against the U.S. dollar.
